# Der Weg des Ritters

An action-RPG in the shape of Diablo, set in the East Prussia of the late
Middle Ages — the amber coast of the Frisches Haff, the Rominten wilderness,
the peat bogs, a fallen Ordensburg, and the sacred grove of Romuva. Built to
be played with two thumbs in a phone browser.

**Everything you see and hear is generated by code.** There are no image files,
no audio files, no sprite sheets, no fonts beyond the system stack, and no
third-party engine or library. Ground materials, trees, ruins, characters,
weapons, the interface, the music and every sound effect are produced at
runtime from noise functions, vector drawing and WebAudio oscillators.

## Running it

Any static file server works — the game is plain ES modules with no build step.

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8099
# then open http://localhost:8099/  (or your machine's LAN address on a phone)
```

It also deploys as-is to any static host (GitHub Pages, Netlify, S3).

**Controls**

| | Touch | Keyboard / mouse |
|---|---|---|
| Move | drag anywhere on the left half | `WASD` / arrows |
| Attack, skills | the four round buttons, bottom right | `1` `2` `3` `4`, or `F` to attack |
| Potion | the flask button | `Q` |
| Bag & character | the pouch icon | `I` |
| Menu / pause | the ☰ icon | `Esc` |

Landscape orientation is expected; the game asks you to rotate in portrait.

## What's in it

- **Three classes.** The Ordensritter builds *Zorn* by hitting things and spends
  it on a shield charge, consecrated ground, and a whirlwind. The Jägerin
  spends *Atem* on piercing shots, bear traps, arrow rain and a shadow-step
  volley. The Bernsteinhexer spends *Mana* on amber shards, a freezing cone,
  called lightning and a reflective ward.
- **Five acts**, each a generated region with its own ground, weather, palette,
  bestiary, camps, shrines, chests and a boss with scripted abilities and
  phases. Finish the fifth and *Die Ewige Jagd* restarts the campaign harder.
- **Loot** with rarities, rolled affixes, and six uniques that change how a
  build plays (chain lightning on hit, a frost nova when you're struck, and so
  on). Upgrades equip themselves so you can keep fighting.
- **Progression** to level 40 with a save that survives closing the tab.

## How the visuals are made

The look comes from four ideas, all in `src/render/`:

1. **Relief-lit materials** (`textures.js`). Each ground material is generated
   as a height field first, then lit with a real surface normal, so grit,
   cracks, moss clumps and cobbles catch light instead of reading as flat
   colour. Every tile is seamless.
2. **Layered, hand-drawn props** (`props.js`). Trees are not triangles: a pine
   is a trunk plus fifty drooping needle fronds, each shaded by its depth in
   the canopy, with a cold moon rim applied to the whole silhouette afterwards.
   Sprites are trimmed to their opaque bounds and pre-scaled to the current
   zoom so drawing them is a straight blit.
3. **Articulated actors** (`actors.js`). Characters are rigs posed in 3D and
   projected through the same 2.5D transform as the world. That is why they can
   face any direction, occlude their own limbs correctly, and swing a weapon
   that travels through a real arc.
4. **A lit, graded frame** (`renderer.js`). Chunked terrain, a half-resolution
   dynamic light map multiplied over the scene and re-added for warm
   overbright, an emissive-only bloom buffer, parallax fog sheets, weather, and
   a baked grade-and-vignette pass.

Resolution and effect quality adapt automatically to whatever frame rate the
device is holding, so the same build looks its best on a fast phone and stays
playable on a slow one.

## Layout

```
index.html            page shell and loading screen
styles.css            the only CSS; the game itself is one canvas
src/core/             math, seeded RNG, input, WebAudio, save
src/render/           noise, palette, materials, props, actors, FX, renderer
src/game/             content tables, world generation, loot, the game loop
src/ui/               HUD, panels, menus
tools/                Playwright drivers for screenshots, benchmarks, autoplay
```

## Development tools

```bash
node tools/play.mjs  out --script fight     # screenshots of a scripted fight
node tools/autoplay.mjs out --acts 5        # a bot plays the campaign for real
node tools/bench.mjs                        # frame rate at each quality tier
node tools/ablate.mjs                       # which render stage costs what
npx eslint .
```

`tools/preview-art.html` and `tools/preview-actors.html` render every material,
prop and character rig on one page, which is the fastest way to iterate on art.
